summary: All five review findings were real and are fixed at the root; none was rejected. The two major ones (provenance test failing; no gapless header) are closed with regression tests. typecheck has 0 errors, `npx vitest run src/audio` gives 231 passed and 2 skipped, and `FOUNDRESS_LONG=1 npx vitest run src/audio/provenance` gives 24 passed (all 36 judged, shipped files byte-identical to a fresh render). All 36 sounds were re-rendered and `check.mjs` passes on every one. The browser stage of `verify:portable` was not re-run after the fixes (another engineer's headless Chrome was running).
verification: npm run typecheck: 0 errors (nothing reported for src/audio or tools/audio).
npx vitest run src/audio: 14 files, 231 passed, 2 skipped (the LONG blocks).

FOUNDRESS_LONG=1 npx vitest run src/audio/provenance (after the final render): 24 passed in 77 s. This covers all 36 checkSpec judgements, the byte-identity of the shipped files against a fresh render, and the reviewer's Xing/Info and decoded-length tests that failed before.

node tools/audio/check.mjs: all 36 ok. Every decoded length equals its rendered length, true peaks are at or below -3.0 dBFS, loops are at their LUFS targets, and seams are inside the limits (test-output/audio-provenance-fix/check2.txt).
measure.ts re-run on the old and new files with no delay offset: no out-of-range centroids. Tables regenerated in test-output/audio-provenance-fix/tables.md and spliced into the report.
ffmpeg decode of ui_click_01.mp3 gives 19404 bytes of float32, which is 4851 samples, the rendered length. It was 6912 samples before the fix.
npm run build:portable: OK, audio pack 8.15 MB with 45 assets, total 27.77 MB. verify-portable.mjs --scan-only --no-build: PASS (logs in test-output/audio-provenance-fix/).

acceptance.criterion: Finding 1: always-on provenance test fails (level slack against the encoder compensation)
acceptance.evidence: check.mjs allows ENCODER_LOSS_DB when it judges PCM only, and judges the decoded file otherwise. New test 'three cheap one-shots meet the level convention on the decoded file' passes, and the whole src/audio suite is green.

acceptance.criterion: Finding 2: new MP3s lack the Xing/Info gapless header
acceptance.evidence: encodeMp3 and decodeMp3 now go through a temporary file. renderMp3 throws if a decoded length differs from the rendered length. The reviewer's two failing tests pass, and the LONG byte-identity test passes.

acceptance.criterion: Finding 3: one-shot loudness metric counted encoder delay and padding; the report blamed the peak for the wrong sounds
acceptance.evidence: The metric is taken on the gapless decoded file. old-levels.json was re-measured (short clips were up to 1.1 LU too quiet) and the sounds were re-rendered, so ui_click_01/02, ui_hover_01 and ui_switch_01 now match the old loudness. The report's peak-limited list is corrected to thud_01, chirp_01/02, ui_click_03 and broom_01/02.

acceptance.criterion: Finding 4: 'before' seam and join numbers measured on a window shifted by 1105 samples
acceptance.evidence: measure.ts no longer applies ENCODER_DELAY. The old files were re-measured and the report tables regenerated (traffic_distant before: jump 2.8, kink 28.2).

acceptance.criterion: Finding 5: nine kept files labelled tier A without the evidence tier A needs
acceptance.evidence: sync-records.mjs writes tier 'A-badge' plus an evidence field for the nine kept files. provenance.test.ts asserts this and that no record is B. Criterion 1 (no tier B) still holds.

acceptance.criterion: Records 'seconds' read 0.16 s for a 0.11 s click
acceptance.evidence: Records now use the decoded duration; a test asserts ui_click_01 is 0.11 s.

acceptance.criterion: Do not weaken the reviewer's tests
acceptance.evidence: All 9 of the reviewer's tests are kept. Only a stale 'FAILS at review time' comment was updated.

notDone: The browser stage of `npm run verify:portable` was not re-run on the re-rendered files because another engineer's headless Chrome was running. The build and the static scan pass; the fixes change file bytes only, not names, count or the pack mechanism. The integration gate should re-run it.

The reviewer's browser loudness scenes were not re-run after the fix (the reviewer ran them on the first version and all passed). The fix changes only the gapless header and the levels of five short clips.

Still open and not in my paths: src/ui/screens/credits/parse.test.ts line 25 still expects the archive.org group. tools/assets/build_manifest.py and process_audio.py are stale for audio. No ear check is possible here.
Not changed: the nine kept OpenGameArt files are labelled A-badge with no saved copy of the author pages. That residual risk is documented, not removed.
notesForIntegrator: Audio file bytes changed again: all 36 replaced mp3 files were re-rendered, and the manifest, records and MANIFEST.md totals were re-synced (public/assets total 19,914,641 B). The portable build was rebuilt (audio pack 8.15 MB), so a fresh `npm run verify:portable` is advisable when no other headless browser is running.
The record field `tier` for the nine kept files is now 'A-badge' (new `evidence` field). Nothing in src or tools reads it besides the provenance tests.
ffmpeg must stay able to write seekable mp3 files to the temp directory (os.tmpdir()). The encoder no longer uses a pipe.

Evidence is in test-output/audio-provenance-fix/ (check2.txt, old.json, new.json, tables.md, build-portable.log, verify-scan.log). The report is docs/design/tasks/audio-provenance-report.md, with a new section 10 covering this review.
